channel.title: LingoPlaytime Blog
channel.description: Practical, research-backed help for raising a bilingual or multilingual toddler: home language plans, late talking, daycare and keeping a minority language alive.

item.title: Language pair guides: first words and a home plan for every pair
item.description: English, German, Spanish, French, Italian and Portuguese in every pairing: sixteen first words side by side, what the two languages share, and where they trip children up.

item.title: Myths about raising a multilingual child, checked against the research
item.description: Does a second language confuse toddlers, cause speech delay or make kids smarter? Common beliefs about raising bilingual and multilingual children, checked against the best studies.

item.title: Which language should you speak to your child? Usually the one you speak best
item.description: Should you speak the local language to help your child at school? Research on parents speaking a second language, native versus fluent input, and where the community language really comes from.

item.title: Raising a child with three or four languages: what the research says
item.description: Can toddlers learn three or four languages? What studies of trilingual children show, how to split the week between languages, and which language needs the most protection.

item.title: Can toddlers learn a language from videos, apps and video calls?
item.description: What experiments show about babies and toddlers learning language from video, audio, apps and video calls, and how sitting with your child changes what they learn.

item.title: How to raise a bilingual child: what actually works in the toddler years
item.description: Raising a bilingual or multilingual toddler? What research says about one parent one language, speaking the minority language at home, and how much each language needs.

item.title: Is my bilingual toddler a late talker? What the research says
item.description: Worried your bilingual toddler is talking late or mixing languages? Research shows bilingualism doesn't cause speech delays. How to count words across languages, and when to get help.

item.title: How to keep your home language alive when daycare starts
item.description: When daycare or school starts, children often switch to the community language. How multilingual families keep a heritage language strong, with research and simple routines.
